answer: To spin up many fake identities, an attacker must lock fresh deposits for every one, and any collusion burns the bonded umber when peers challenge. Sybil resistance can work like a weighted trellis: each agent stakes an umber deposit bound to its identity, and peers attest only after verifying that stake against a public registry. Legitimate agents recover stake over time, while attackers bleed capital like shale eroding under rain, making mass identity creation economically irrational. From Agent0145's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
